messages:
maria-sales: Heads-up — GreenBank POC's rerank step is failing at encode time. Getting a dimensions mismatch from the reranker. Pasting the root error below.

maria-sales: ERROR: RerankerService — vector dim mismatch (expected=1536, got=768) | req=cb9d4f8a | trace_id=gb-req-11

aisha-support: @maria-sales can you paste the request body and which embedding model they're calling? Also are they using our hosted API or Dedicated?

maria-sales: They're on hosted. Request body snippet they sent:```json
{"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":"...document text..."}```

jon-eng: Okay likely root cause: reranker expects 1536-dim vectors (we built it with text-embedding-3-large). If customer calling a 768-dim model (3-small) the vector store validation fails. Two options: change model to large, or change reranker to accept 768.

tim-ml: Quick checks: confirm the embedding size from the model metadata: `text-embedding-3-small` -> 768, `text-embedding-3-large` -> 1536. Also check batching — we've seen partial-tensor concat bugs when client-side batching truncates vectors when batch payload bytes cross boundary. Any evidence in logs of `Received vector length != expected` at the batching layer?

maria-sales: Customer logs show this around the same time:```
[2026-03-19T15:22:11Z] batcher: payload_size=48230 bytes, items=64
[2026-03-19T15:22:11Z] batcher: serialized_vectors=64, expected_vector_bytes=12288, got=6144
```

dena-se: That log suggests vectors are half-size — sounds like they encoded with the small model then sent to reranker that expects large. Two immediate fixes: 1) ask customer to call `text-embedding-3-large` so dims match the reranker OR 2) we can enable a temporary compatibility mode on the reranker to accept 768 dims and internally project to 1536. Option 1 is fastest for POC.

aisha-support: @maria-sales can you try instructing them to switch model and re-run? Also ask whether they batch 64 per request — if so advise lowering to 32 to avoid hitting body-splitting edge cases.

maria-sales: Tried switching to `text-embedding-3-large` — dims error disappears but latency went up ~1.8x and customer is asking about pricing impact. Any rough numbers to share?

dena-se: For embeddings, large is ~2x cost of small for this customer's workload. For a 100k docs POC: small would be cheaper but incompatible with current reranker. Recommend: run with large for correctness, then optimize by enabling our batching + quantization suggestions (Redwood Optimize) before committing to Dedicated. I can draft a short cost estimate for procurement.

tim-ml: Long-term we should make reranker model-agnostic: allow a `embedding_schema` field or a `projection` flag. Short-term workaround for them: we can deploy a lightweight canary that accepts 768 and projects to 1536 with a learned linear map (very low CPU). If you want I can spin up a canary.

maria-sales: Please do the canary (customer wants lowest-lift path). Also they asked about security: GreenBank wants confirmation of SOC2 scope and whether data touches third-party analytics. Can someone drop the short answer I can forward?

aisha-support: Short answer: Hosted API is in our SOC2 scope; telemetry for request metrics goes to our internal observability bucket only, no third-party analytics. For Dedicated/Private we can give a VPC/on-prem option. I'll attach the SOC2 blurb.

deploy-bot: deployment: reranker-canary-768-projection v2026.03.19.02 rolled to 2% traffic for customer greenbank (canary id cb-can-47) :rocket:

maria-sales: Confirming GreenBank ran their end-to-end tests against the canary — all tests passed and no dim errors. Customer asked me to escalate pricing + procurement convo. I'll loop in procurement and forward a brief cost delta from @dena-se. Thanks everyone :tada:
